statements.attributed: fabrication of high‐entropy Prussian blue analogs
statements.quote: Ma et al. first reported the fabrication of high‐entropy Prussian blue analogs (HE‐PBA) by integrating Mn, Co, Ni, Fe, and Cu ions into the framework structure via the co‐precipitation method (Figure 4a). Although the classification of PBA as MOF is a topic of debate, we include it in this review, since the functionality and morphology of PBA compounds resemble classical MOFs.

statements.attributed: fabrication of Prussian white analogs
statements.quote: Recently, applying the co‐precipitation method, a series of Prussian white analogs (PW) with up to six metal cations were fabricated by He et al. As shown in Figure 4d, it is evident that six metal ions (Mn, Fe, Ni, Cu, Co, and Cd) collectively share the high‐entropy metal sites, while Fe1 ions occupy the Fe sites, which constructs the framework structure of high‐entropy PW (HE‐PW) through coordinating with the cyanide group.

statements.attributed: synthesis of high‐entropy zeolitic imidazolate framework
statements.quote: Xu et al. prepared a high‐entropy zeolitic imidazolate framework (HE‐ZIF) through ball milling CdO, CuO, ZnO, Ni(OAc)2, Co(OAc)2, and excess 2‐methylimidazole at room temperature for 120 min (Figure 5a). According to the results of EDS mapping (Figure 5b), it is clear that Cd2+, Cu2+, Zn2+, Ni2+, and Co2+ are homogeneously distributed in HE‐ZIF.

statements.attributed: synthesis of HE‐MOF for OER
statements.quote: Yao et al. synthesized HE‐MOF as a working electrode for OER through the coordination of Mn, Fe, Ni, Co, and Cu metal ions with organic ligands of 2,5‐thiophenedicarboxylic acid (TDC) and 4,4‐bipyridine (BIPY). Benefiting from the integration of multiple cations, lattice distortion was induced in HE‐MOF, which modifies the coordination environments at catalytic metal sites and generates oxygen vacancies (Figure 6a), thus leading to enhanced binding energy between the catalytic surface and intermediates, as well as improved electrocatalytic activity compared to conventional Co‐TDC‐BIPY MOF.

statements.attributed: improved OER activity
statements.quote: In addition to direct use as electrocatalysts for OER, HE‐MOFs have been employed as precursors to fabricate diverse HEMs, such as HEAs, HEOs, HESs, and HEPs, which also exhibit great potential in catalyzing water splitting.[ , , , ] For example, Wang et al. devised a MOF‐templated strategy to prepare a series of nanosized CoNiCuMnAl/C (HEAs/C) by adjusting the stirring time of the precursor solution. The OER activity of as‐obtained HEAs/C was examined in an O2‐saturated 1 m KOH electrolyte and compared to the commercial RuO2 catalyst.

statements.attributed: improved OER activity
statements.quote: Miao et al. reported the synthesis of hollow‐structured and polyhedron‐shaped ZnFeNiCuCoRu‐O using MOF as a sacrificial template via the ion exchange method. When applied as catalyst for OER, the ZnFeNiCuCoRu‐O demonstrated impressive catalytic activity in full pH range, with an overpotential of 170, 215, and 270 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2 in 1.0 m KOH (pH ≈ 14), 0.5 m H2SO4 (pH ≈ 0), and 1 m PBS (pH ≈ 7) aqueous solutions, respectively, surpassing its quinary and denary counterparts as well as the commercial RuO2 (Figure 7a–c).

statements.attributed: photocatalytic hydrogen evolution
statements.quote: A noble‐metal‐free MnNiCoZn‐based HE‐MOF was investigated by Qi et al., and reported for the first time as a photocatalyst for hydrogen evolution.

statements.attributed: synthesis of HE‐ZIF for CO2 fixation
statements.quote: Xu et al. synthesized HE‐ZIF with a uniform distribution of cations through ball grinding at ambient temperature. The catalytic activity of HE‐ZIF, single‐metal ZIFs (including Zn‐ZIF (ZIF‐8), Co‐ZIF (ZIF‐67), and Cd‐ZIF (Cd‐ZIF‐8)), and a physical mixture of these three single‐metal ZIFs (PM‐ZIF) was evaluated under 10 bar CO2 pressure at 100 °C for 8 h.

statements.attributed: fabrication of NH3⋅H2O‐etched HE‐PBA
statements.quote: Xu et al. developed NH3⋅H2O‐etched HE‐PBA (HE‐PBA‐e) through a simple co‐precipitation method followed by an etching treatment. Compared to pristine HE‐PBA, HE‐PBA‐e surprisingly demonstrated a modified electronic structure with a higher proportion of Co3+ and Ni3+ species, which are known to be effective catalytical centers.

statements.attributed: developed Na1.19(Fe0.2Mn0.2Ni0.2Cu0.2Co0.2)[Fe(CN)6]0.79□0.21 (HE‐PBA) as cathode material in sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs)

statements.quote: Ma et al. developed Na1.19(Fe0.2Mn0.2Ni0.2Cu0.2Co0.2)[Fe(CN)6]0.79□0.21 (HE‐PBA) through a facile co‐precipitation method and used it as cathode material in sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) for the first time. As illustrated in Figure 10a, compared with the medium‐entropy PBAs counterparts, the HE‐PBA displayed an improved Na+ storage capacity (an initial capacity of 100 mAh g−1 at a current density of 0.1 A g−1) and superior cycling stability (capacity retention of 94% after 150th cycles).

statements.attributed: synthesized a series of PWs via a co‐precipitation approach at room temperature and explored their electrochemical performance as cathodes in SIBs
statements.quote: Very recently, He et al. synthesized a series of PWs via a co‐precipitation approach at room temperature and explored their electrochemical performance as cathodes in SIBs. The as‐obtained Na1.65(Mn0.4Fe0.12Ni0.12Cu0.12Co0.12Cd0.12)[Fe(CN)6]0.92□0.08 (HE‐PW) cathode exhibited superior electrochemical performance compared to its medium‐entropy (ME‐), low‐entropy (LE‐), and conventional manganese (Mn‐) PW counterparts (Figure 10e).

statements.attributed: the main limitation of the practical applications of SCs is related to their inherently low energy density
statements.quote: Supercapacitors (SCs) with the merits of ultrafast charge–discharge rate, wide operating temperature range (−10 to 80 °C), and long cycle life (>105 cycles), are regarded as one of the most promising and efficient energy storage technologies, which have attracted numerous attentions in high‐power‐demanding devices. The main limitation of the practical applications of SCs is related to their inherently low energy density. Consequently, the crucial factor in unleashing their complete potential lies in the design and development of high‐performance novel electrode materials.

statements.attributed: utilized DFT calculations to reveal the underlying mechanisms connecting the high‐entropy strategy to the outstanding catalytic or energy storage performance
statements.quote: As shown in Figure 13a, several studies have utilized DFT calculations to reveal the underlying mechanisms connecting the high‐entropy strategy to the outstanding catalytic or energy storage performance.[ , , ] However, due to the compositional complexity and highly disordered lattice structures of high‐entropy systems, as well as the time‐consuming calculation process, DFT is generally applicable to property calculations of HE‐MOFs with specific compositions but provides only limited guidance for experimental screening across larger compositional landscapes.

statements.attributed: proposed a data‐efficient multi‐objective Bayesian optimization framework driven by the ML surrogate model for discovering novel catalysts composed of higher‐dimensional constituent elements
statements.quote: Recent advances in machine learning (ML), however, offer a promising pathway to accelerate the discovery of novel multi‐component high‐entropy systems.[ , , ] Xu et al. proposed a data‐efficient multi‐objective Bayesian optimization framework driven by the ML surrogate model for discovering novel catalysts composed of higher‐dimensional constituent elements (Figure 13b). The designed method can simultaneously optimize catalytic activity, mixing entropy, and manufacturability within a vast design space, ultimately presenting a series of promising candidates.

statements.attributed: presented a MOF discovery strategy using ML models to directly predict the synthesis conditions based on MOF crystal structures
statements.quote: Similarly, Luo et al. presented a MOF discovery strategy using ML models to directly predict the synthesis conditions based on MOF crystal structures (Figure 13c), which provides a highly valuable tool for the advancement of the MOF community. Therefore, although there are currently no reports on the direct use of ML models for HE‐MOFs, it is quite certain that ML can also be applied to design multi‐metal HE‐MOFs within a higher‐dimensional composition space and optimize their physicochemical properties for catalysis and energy applications.
